get_loinc_answers.description: Get the answers a LOINC question offers, in order, each with its LOINC answer code and score: 'Not at all' to 'Nearly every day' for a PHQ-9 question, for example. Every answer list the question has comes back, with the forms each is used in. A question that takes a free value comes back with no answer list. No API key required.

look_up_codes.description: Check up to 100 codes from one code set at once, such as the diagnosis codes on a claim or the test codes in a lab feed, and get each one's name. Works with ICD-10-CM, ICD-11, ICD-9-CM, HCPCS, LOINC, RxNorm ingredient ids, HPO and UCUM. Each comes back with its definition, synonyms (including words for patients), the more general terms it sits under and a link. No API key required.

phenotypes.comment: A type of electrographic seizure has been proposed in neonates which does not have a clinical correlate, it is electrographic only. The term epilepsy is not used to describe recurrent febrile seizures. Epilepsy presumably reflects an abnormally reduced seizure threshold.
phenotypes.definition: A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain
phenotypes.name: Seizure

phenotypes.comment: This term describes the initial semiology of the seizure without specifying whether the onset is focal or generalized. Thus it can be used for coding atonic seizures when the onset is not known.
phenotypes.definition: Atonic seizure is a type of motor seizure characterized by a sudden loss or diminution of muscle tone without apparent preceding myoclonic or tonic event lasting about 1 to 2 seconds, involving head, trunk, jaw, or limb musculature
phenotypes.name: Atonic seizure

description: Search and look up the medical code sets the U.S. National Library of Medicine serves: ICD-10-CM, ICD-11 and ICD-9-CM diagnosis codes, HCPCS codes, LOINC lab tests, questions and forms with their answer lists, RxTerms drugs with their strengths and RxNorm ids, drug ingredients, everyday names for conditions and surgeries with their codes, NPI providers and organizations, UCUM units, HPO phenotypes, HGNC genes and ClinVar variants. Check a batch of codes from a claim or a lab feed in one step, turn a code into its description or a term into its code, list a questionnaire's questions and answers, or find out who a provider is from their NPI. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No account or API key required.
